newsitem.title: ITALY: Toro sees 1997 result in line with 1996.
newsitem.headline: Toro sees 1997 result in line with 1996.

text.p: Italian insurer Toro Assicurazioni SpA, part of the Fiat group, said it hopes to see 1997 results around 1996 levels despite lower group net profit last year.

In the first quarter this year, group premium income was up 15.9 percent to 1.003 trillion lire, Toro said in a statement. "For the whole year forecasts are positive with the aim for results at 1996 levels," it said.

It said 1996 group net profit slipped to 152.8 billion lire from 166.5 billion in 1995 although pre-tax profit was 231.9 billion lire against 224.5 billion, with operating profit of 241.3 billion compared to 195.6 billion.
Toro said net profit was slightly lower due to lower extraordinary income and greater fiscal charges.
Parent company net profit in 1996 was 129.1 billion lire against 149.6 billion, with a proposed dividend of 440 lire per ordinary and preference share up from 400 lire in 1995.

Group premium income in 1996 rose 46.7 percent in 1996 to 3.74 trillion lire while investments were 27.4 percent up at 9.07 trillion lire. Technical reserves rose 39.7 percent to 7.68 trillion lire and net assets rose to 2.015 trillion lire from 1.904 trillion.
